q8.answer: Counts live in one shared Redis (replicated primary with failover), keyed rl:{customerId}:{floor(redisNow/60)}, so every gateway instance reads and writes the same number. Old counts are removed by a 120 s EXPIRE set when the key is first created; the window number in the key name also keeps stale keys from affecting later windows.

q9.answer: Budget resets when the fixed calendar minute (by the Redis clock) rolls over, because the next window uses a new key starting at zero. There is no gradual recovery or refund; rejected requests cost nothing, but passed ones stay counted until the window ends.

q10.answer: The check-and-increment runs as a single atomic Lua script in Redis, which executes scripts one at a time. So two instances cannot both read a count below the limit and both take the last slot; the second sees the incremented count and is rejected.

q11.answer: Retry-After is 60 - (redisNow mod 60), computed inside the script from the Redis clock: whole seconds until the current fixed window ends, ranging 1 to 60. It is sent only on 429 responses.

q12.answer: No retry: the gateway makes one call with a 50 ms timeout, and on error or timeout it forwards the request, emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and every later request tries Redis again (no circuit breaker in v1). The client gets the backend response with no X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining headers, since the count is unknown.
